description.undefined: Application ontology for automotive circular-economy product, material, sustainability, usage, dismantling, engineering and transactional data aligned to PMDCore and BFO 2020.

IAO_0000115.value: An information content entity that is the outcome of a dubbing process and is used to refer to one instance of entity shared by a group of people to refer to that individual entity.

comment.en: Sep 29, 2016: The current definition has been amended from the previous version: "A proper name is an information content entity that is the outcome of a dubbing process and is used to refer to one instance of entity shared by a group of people to refer to that individual entity." to more accuratly reflect the necessary and sufficient condition on the class. (MB)

example.value: 4 vol.% nitric acid solution, Styrene-Butadiene-Styrene (SBS) Block Copolymer with 50 vol.% of both styrene and butadiene

definition.value: A business partner number that identifies the owner of a data asset, material card, or digital twin record.

example.value: A BPNL recorded as the owner of a simulation material card.

definition.value: function of an organization to partake in for profit activities as prescribed by the objectives specified by that organization

intensive quality epitomizing the distinct phases in the microscopic structure of a metallic material.

comment.en: ferrite, austenite, martensite, etc.

plan specification that prescribes a packaging process
plan specification that has one or more supply chain objective specifications as parts and that prescribes a supply chain process

example.value: A sorted batch of dismantled polymer components sent to a recycler.

example.value: An empty recycling container with a mass of 3000 kg.

definition.value: A volume quality that quantifies the internal capacity of a container.

example.value: A roll-off container with a capacity of 20000 L.

definition.value: (Elucidation) A continuant is an entity that persists, endures, or continues to exist through time while maintaining its identity

example.value: A human being; a tennis ball; a cave; a region of space; someone's temperature

definition.value: (Elucidation) An occurrent is an entity that unfolds itself in time or it is the start or end of such an entity or it is a temporal or spatiotemporal region

example.value: As for process, history, process boundary, spatiotemporal region, zero-dimensional temporal region, one-dimensional temporal region, temporal interval, temporal instant.

definition.value: (Elucidation) An entity is anything that exists or has existed or will exist

example.value: Julius Caesar; the Second World War; your body mass index; Verdi's Requiem

definition.value: (Elucidation) A spatial region is a continuant entity that is a continuant part of the spatial projection of a portion of spacetime at a given time

example.value: As for zero-dimensional spatial region, one-dimensional spatial region, two-dimensional spatial region, three-dimensional spatial region

definition.value: b is an independent continuant =Def b is a continuant & there is no c such that b specifically depends on c or b generically depends on c

example.value: An atom; a molecule; an organism; a heart; a chair; the bottom right portion of a human torso; a leg; the interior of your mouth; a spatial region; an orchestra

definition.value: (Elucidation) A temporal region is an occurrent over which processes can unfold

example.value: As for zero-dimensional temporal region and one-dimensional temporal region

definition.value: A quantitative indication of the doubt about a measurement result, expressing the range within which the true value is expected to lie.
A datum that represents a date or time interval associated with another specification.
A melt temperature that specifies the lower allowed or observed temperature of input melt in a manufacturing process.

example.value: A minimum melt temperature of 270 degC in an injection molding process window.

comment.en: Expected value datatype: xsd:float; expected unit: degC.

definition.value: A temperature quality that inheres in a mold during a manufacturing process.

example.value: A mold temperature of 90 degC specified for processing a glass-fiber-reinforced polyamide.

comment.en: Expected value datatype: xsd:float; expected unit: degC.

definition.value: A mold temperature that specifies the upper allowed or observed temperature of a mold during a manufacturing process.

example.value: A maximum mold temperature of 100 degC in an injection molding process window.

comment.en: Expected value datatype: xsd:float; expected unit: degC.

A mold temperature that specifies the lower allowed or observed temperature of a mold during a manufacturing process.

example.value: A minimum mold temperature of 80 degC in an injection molding process window.

supplier role held by a person or organization when it offers to sell or provide a commercial service
service provider role that is held by a business organization or person when it provides a logistics service
agent role held by a person or organization when it buys a product or a service

collection of material entities delivered to a receiver's location that have undergone the same dispatch and receipt processes
business function that is realized in a transportation service
role that someone or something has when they act on behalf of a person, engineered system or a group of agents

example.value: A melt temperature of 280 degC specified for processing PA66-GF25.

process of taking up elctromagnetic radiation by a material entity

IAO_0000115.value: A chemical entity is a physical entity of interest in chemistry including molecular entities, parts thereof, and chemical substances.

definition.value: role held by a number of uniquely identified material entities when they participate in some supply chain processes or production processes while some agent observes them and collects information about them for future retrieval
role held by a geospatial site when it is the location of some material entity at some time or the site of some process
(Elucidation) A temporal interval is a one-dimensional temporal region that is continuous, thus without gaps or breaks

example.value: The year 2018.

definition.value: (Elucidation) A temporal instant is a zero-dimensional temporal region that has no proper temporal part

example.value: The millennium

definition.value: role held by an agent that is a part of a supply chain system when it supplies material products or commercial services to other agents in the supply chain system
role held by a person or business organization when it buys some product from a distributor and resells them to retailers
location role held by a geospatial site when it is the site some supply chain process
role held by a material entity that is intended to be sold, or has been bought, or has been supplied
role held by a material entity when it is acquired by an organizational entity with some plan to transform or modify it into intermediate-level components or substances or into a product

An object aggregate that consists of two or more bonded materials with dissimilar physical or chemical properties which are used to complement each other where the parts remain seperate and distinct in the resulting object aggregate.

example.value:
carbon fibre reinforced polymer
laminated glass
wood
hard metal composites for abrasive tools

IAO_0000115.value: A person or organization that has a manufacturer role.
A value specification that is specifies one category out of a fixed number of nominal categories
A value specification that consists of two parts: a numeral and a unit label
An information content entity that specifies a value within a classification scheme or on a quantitative scale.

definition.value: A state of matter boundary is a phase boundary that is realized by the transition from one aggregate state to another aggregate state.
The deformation is a process describing a change in the shape, size, or structure of a material often under the influence of stress or force.
The density is a universal intensive quality representing the unit mass of a portion of matter per unit volume.
A natural process that operates within the Earth system to transform, transport, or deform Earth materials, thereby changing Earth structures and landforms
an intensive quality describing the number of defects per unit volume or area in a material, which can affect its mechanical and electronic properties
A process that involves the systematic use of computational methods and tools to perform simulations, analyses, or data transformations to achieve specific scientific or engineering goals.

Ein Prozess, der die systematische Verwendung von rechnerischen Methoden und Werkzeugen umfasst, um Simulationen, Analysen oder Datenumwandlungen durchzuführen, um spezifische wissenschaftliche oder technische Ziele zu erreichen.
an intensive qualtty of a crystal that embodies the periodic geometric arrangement of entities in a crystal lattice.

comment.en: The finite set of periodic geometric arrangements is described e.g. by the 14 possible Bravais Lattices in three-dimensional space.

definition.value: b is a specifically dependent continuant =Def b is a continuant & there is some independent continuant c which is not a spatial region & which is such that b specifically depends on c

example.value: (with one bearer) The mass of this tomato; the pink colour of a medium rare piece of grilled filet mignon at its centre; the smell of this portion of mozzarella; the disposition of this fish to decay; the role of being a doctor; the function of this heart to pump blood; the shape of this hole
(with multiple bearers) John's love for Mary; the ownership relation between John and this statue; the relation of authority between John and his subordinates

definition.value: A process chain is a process that 'has continuant part' subprocesses S1...Sn where S1...Sn precede each other and where some object or object aggregate that are output of Sn are then input to Sn+1.
The heat capacity is a thermal property describing the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a material by a given amount.
an extensive quality of material entities which manifests as a capacity to perform work (such as causing motion or the interaction of molecules)
(Elucidation) A fiat object part b is a material entity & such that if b exists then it is continuant part of some object c & demarcated from the remainder of c by one or more fiat surfaces

example.value: The upper and lower lobes of the left lung; the dorsal and ventral surfaces of the body; the Western hemisphere of the Earth; the FMA:regional parts of an intact human body

definition.value: An extensive quality is a quality that inheres in only object or object aggregate or fiat object part or chemical entity and is dependent on the bearers (system-) size.
The hardness is a mechanical property used as a measure of a material's resistance to localized plastic deformation, often tested by indentation or scratch methods.

(Elucidation) A role b is a realizable entity such that b exists because there is some single bearer that is in some special physical, social, or institutional set of circumstances in which this bearer does not have to be & b is not such that, if it ceases to exist, then the physical make-up of the bearer is thereby changed

example.value: The priest role; the student role; the role of subject in a clinical trial; the role of a stone in marking a property boundary; the role of a boundary to demarcate two neighbouring administrative territories; the role of a building in serving as a military target

definition.value: The bulk is a fiat object part that describes the volume or mass of material considered as a whole, often in contrast to surface or interface phenomena.

(Elucidation) A site is a three-dimensional immaterial entity whose boundaries either (partially or wholly) coincide with the boundaries of one or more material entities or have locations determined in relation to some material entity

example.value: A hole in a portion of cheese; a rabbit hole; the Grand Canyon; the Piazza San Marco; the kangaroo-joey-containing hole of a kangaroo pouch; your left nostril (a fiat part - the opening - of your left nasal cavity); the lumen of your gut; the hold of a ship; the interior of the trunk of your car; hole in an engineered floor joist

definition.value: (Elucidation) An object aggregate is a material entity consisting exactly of a plurality (≥1) of objects as member parts which together form a unit

example.value: The aggregate of the musicians in a symphony orchestra and their instruments; the aggregate of bearings in a constant velocity axle joint; the nitrogen atoms in the atmosphere; a collection of cells in a blood biobank

definition.value: Volume is a three dimensional size.

IAO_0000115.value: A biological process is the execution of a genetically-encoded biological module or program. It consists of all the steps required to achieve the specific biological objective of the module. A biological process is accomplished by a particular set of molecular functions carried out by specific gene products (or macromolecular complexes), often in a highly regulated manner and in a particular temporal sequence.

definition.value: is a process that occurs as a reaction to change of elctric field or movement of charges and produces a magnetic field
is a process in which forces, moments, or imposed displacements to objects or object aggregates occur and/or the equivalent (stresses, strains) to materials or portions of matter
is a process in which transfer of thermal energy between or within material entities occurs
(Elucidation) A spatiotemporal region is an occurrent that is an occurrent part of spacetime

example.value: The spatiotemporal region occupied by the development of a cancer tumour; the spatiotemporal region occupied by an orbiting satellite

definition.value: (Elucidation) A realizable entity is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in some independent continuant which is not a spatial region & which is of a type some instances of which are realized in processes of a correlated type

example.value: The role of being a doctor; the role of this boundary to delineate where Utah and Colorado meet; the function of your reproductive organs; the disposition of your blood to coagulate; the disposition of this piece of metal to conduct electricity

definition.value: (Elucidation) p is a process means p is an occurrent that has some temporal proper part and for some time t, p has some material entity as participant

example.value: An act of selling; the life of an organism; a process of sleeping; a process of cell-division; a beating of the heart; a process of meiosis; the taxiing of an aircraft; the programming of a computer

definition.value: (Elucidation) A disposition b is a realizable entity such that if b ceases to exist then its bearer is physically changed & b's realization occurs when and because this bearer is in some special physical circumstances & this realization occurs in virtue of the bearer's physical make-up

example.value: An atom of element X has the disposition to decay to an atom of element Y; the cell wall is disposed to transport cellular material through endocytosis and exocytosis; certain people have a predisposition to colon cancer; children are innately disposed to categorize objects in certain ways

definition.value: Thermodynamic activity is a relational quality that inheres between a chemical species and a non-ideal solution and represents the effective concentration of the species accounting for particle interactions.
(Elucidation) A quality is a specifically dependent continuant that, in contrast to roles and dispositions, does not require any further process in order to be realized

example.value: The colour of a tomato; the ambient temperature of this portion of air; the length of the circumference of your waist; the shape of your nose; the shape of your nostril; the mass of this piece of gold

IAO_0000115.value: An independent continuant that is spatially extended whose identity is independent of that of other entities and can be maintained through time.

definition.value: (Elucidation) A material entity is an independent continuant has some portion of matter as continuant part

example.value: A human being; the undetached arm of a human being; an aggregate of human beings

definition.value: An injection molding machine is a device used to produce plastic parts by injecting molten plastic into molds under high pressure.
Eine Spritzgießmaschine ist ein Gerät, das verwendet wird, um Kunststoffteile durch Einspritzen von geschmolzenem Kunststoff in Formen unter hohem Druck herzustellen.
an intensive quality of a thermodynamic system describing the energy change associated with the addition of a small quantity of a substance to a system at constant temperature and pressure.

The chemical composition is an intensive quality of a portion of matter which describes the types and proportions of pure chemical elements in the portion of matter, and it is a subject of some chemical composition data item.

comment.en:
See the editor note of composition to understand the difference between composition and chemical composition.

See the pattern example of composition to underatand the difference between composition and proportion.

definition.value: (Elucidation) A generically dependent continuant is an entity that exists in virtue of the fact that there is at least one of what may be multiple copies which is the content or the pattern that multiple copies would share

example.value: The pdf file on your laptop; the pdf file that is a copy thereof on my laptop; the sequence of this protein molecule; the sequence that is a copy thereof in that protein molecule; the content that is shared by a string of dots and dashes written on a page and the transmitted Morse code signal; the content of a sentence; an engineering blueprint

definition.value: an extensive quality of a material entity that describes its spatial extend.
Mass is fundamental extensive quality.

comment.en: Mass is relevant in such processes as gravitation, acceleration, etc.

definition.value: An intensive quality is a quality that inheres in only portion of matter and thus is independent of the bearers (system-) size.
(Elucidation) An object is a material entity which manifests causal unity & is of a type instances of which are maximal relative to the sort of causal unity manifested

example.value: An organism; a fish tank; a planet; a laptop; a valve; a block of marble; an ice cube

definition.value: p is a process boundary =Def p is a temporal part of a process & p has no proper temporal parts

example.value: The boundary between the 2nd and 3rd year of your life

definition.value: (Elucidation) A function is a disposition that exists in virtue of its bearer's physical make-up & this physical make-up is something the bearer possesses because it came into being either through evolution (in the case of natural biological entities) or through intentional design (in the case of artefacts) in order to realize processes of a certain sort

example.value: The function of a hammer to drive in nails; the function of a heart pacemaker to regulate the beating of a heart through electricity

definition.value: A lot is an object aggregate whose parts are output of the same production process.
change of temperature is a process in which a particpant changes its temperature
Optical property which describes the bending of light as it passes from one medium into another due to a change in the light’s speed.

comment.en: e.g., air into glass

definition.value: (Elucidation) A one-dimensional temporal region is a temporal region that is a whole that has a temporal interval and zero or more temporal intervals and temporal instants as parts

example.value: The temporal region during which a process occurs

definition.value: Molar proportion is the proportion which quantifies the entities count of the part in relation to the entities count of the whole.

example.value:
The molar ratio of hydrogen gas H2 molecules to water H2O molecules is 1/1 in the oxyhydrogen reaction. The molar ratio of oxygen molecules O2 to water molecules is 2/1.
The molar ratio of carbon dioxide to average atmosphere air is 420 ppm as of 2022 AD.

definition.value: Volume proportion is a proportion which quantifies the volume of the part relative to the volume of the whole.
A proportion is a relational quality between two entities (the whole and the part) which quantifies the relation between the whole and its part.
Mass proportion is a proportion which quantifies the mass of the part relative to the mass of the whole.
A polycrystal is a connected material entity aggregate that consists of multiple crystal grains joined through crystallographic interfaces.
An intensive quality describing the lower length scale object aggregate (grains) that is part of the material.
The aggregate state value is a categorical value specification that specifies value of the aggregate state quality.
A gaseous state where the gas entities are atoms.
A state with strong bindings between entities that do not transmit shear force.
An aggregate state where the entities are atom nuclei and have no bonds.
A state that exhibits suprafluid and solid properties.

A state with frictionless binding that transmits no shear force between entities.

A state where the entities have no bonding.

The temperature is a fundamental intensive quality representing the average atomic or molcular movement or vibration of a portion of matter.

comment.en: The concept refers to an absolute temperature, not to be mistaken with temperature difference.

definition.value: an intensive quality representing the physical state of a material, such as solid, liquid, or gasous
is the process of movement of charged particles
A thermal property is a material property representing attributes of a material that describe its behavior under temperature changes, such as thermal conductivity and expansion.
The ASTM grain size is a quality that is measured through a process that follows the ASTM standard.
An intensive quality that quantifies water vapor content in air surrounding a material.

example.value: 50% Relative Humidity (standard conditioning atmosphere).

comment.en: Relevant for polyamides because moisture uptake changes mechanical properties.

definition.value: A stiffness that quantifies the ratio of flexural stress to flexural strain.

example.value: Flexural modulus of 8500 MPa for PA66-GF30.

comment.en: Standard metric for stiffness in plastics (ISO 178).

definition.value: Ein Datenverarbeitungsprozess, der das Verhalten eines Systems im Laufe der Zeit mit mathematischen oder rechnerischen Techniken modelliert
A computing process that models the behavior of a system over time using mathematical or computational techniques.

example.value: 250 MPa for a high-performance composite.

comment.en: Relevant for snap-fit joints in automotive interiors.

definition.value: A plan specification that defines the quality assessment criteria applied to a reused, repaired, remanufactured, or recycled product or component.

example.value: VDI 4080 used as the assessment standard for reuse quality.

definition.value: A quality of a product or component indicating whether its mounting points, clips, tabs, or attachment features are intact and functional.

example.value: A bumper bracket with all mounting tabs undamaged.

definition.value: A quality of a product, component, or material surface indicating the degree to which it is free from oil, dust, residues, and other contaminants.

example.value: A cleaned polymer surface acceptable for adhesive bonding during reuse preparation.

definition.value: A temporal interval required or estimated to repair a specified damage or defect on a product or component.

example.value: The time needed to repair a paint scratch and small dent on a door panel.

definition.value: A strength that quantifies material resistance to fracture under impact loading.

example.value: 45 kJ/m^2 notched impact strength for a bumper material.

comment.en: Often measured via Charpy or Izod notched impact tests.

definition.value: A thermal property that quantifies fractional length change per unit temperature change.

example.value: CLTE measured parallel and normal to fiber orientation in a reinforced polymer part.

comment.en: Used to calculate dimensional change in assemblies that combine materials with different thermal expansion behavior.

IAO_0000115.value: A planned process that has the objective to produce information about a material entity (the evaluant) by examining it.

definition.value: A heat capacity that quantifies heat required to raise the temperature of unit mass of a substance by one temperature unit.

example.value: A specific heat capacity of 1700 J kg^-1 K^-1 for polypropylene.

comment.en: Expected value datatype: xsd:float; expected unit: J kg^-1 K^-1.

definition.value: A quality that records the number of cracks observed on a product, component, coating, or material surface.

example.value: Two cracks recorded in the paint layer during dismantling inspection.

definition.value: A quality of a sheet metal or body component indicating the presence or extent of dents or deformations that impair the component shape.

example.value: A quarter panel with two visible dents after vehicle use.

definition.value: A quality that quantifies the surface area of visible damage on a product, component, coating, or material surface.

example.value: A paint damage area of 50 square centimeters on a door panel.

definition.value: A quality of a painted product or component indicating damage to the paintwork, such as scratches, chips, cracks, or coating loss.

example.value: Stone-chip damage on a painted bumper cover.

definition.value: A viscosity that quantifies resistance to flow under shear deformation.

example.value: Viscosity curve data required for Moldflow simulation.

comment.en: Expected value datatype: xsd:float; expected unit: Pa.s.

definition.value: A phase boundary temperature at which the amorphous phase of a polymer changes between glassy and rubbery states.

example.value: A glass transition temperature of about 50 degC for dry PA66.

comment.en: Below Tg, the amorphous phase is frozen; above Tg, polymer chains have mobility.

definition.value: An intensive quality that quantifies a fluid material's resistance to flow.

example.value: The melt viscosity of polypropylene at 230 degC.

comment.en: Expected value datatype: xsd:float; expected unit: Pa.s.

example.value: BPNL00000003AY2 (Example BPN).

definition.value: A mechanical property that quantifies specimen strain at rupture.

example.value: 3% strain at break for a glass-filled polyamide.

definition.value: A batch identifier assigned to a material batch for traceability.

comment.en: Expected value datatype: xsd:string; expected unit: not specified.

definition.value: A site at which a manufacturer carries out production, assembly, treatment, storage, or related industrial operations.

example.value: A specific plant where a material batch or component was produced.

example.value: A Catena-X BPNL identifier for a supplier legal entity.

definition.value: An identifier assigned to an individual vehicle according to a vehicle identification number scheme.

example.value: A 17-character vehicle identification number used in a dismantling record.

definition.value: An identifier that records the model designation of a vehicle type as defined by a manufacturer.

example.value: A manufacturer-specific vehicle model name used in a product data record.

definition.value: An identifier that records a standard or supplier designation for a material composition.

example.value: PA66-GF25

definition.value: An identifier assigned to a material entity, material batch, material grade, or material data record.

example.value: A material twin identifier used in data exchange.

comment.en: Expected value datatype: xsd:string; expected unit: not specified.

definition.value: An identifier assigned by a manufacturer to a product, component, material grade, or material batch in its own system.

example.value: A manufacturer code for a specific polymer grade.

comment.en: Expected value datatype: xsd:string; expected unit: not specified.

definition.value: An identifier that records the manufacturer name, brand name, or trade name used for a material or product.

example.value: Zytel or Durethan used as a material trade name.

definition.value: An identifier that records the name by which a manufacturer is referred to in a data exchange, contract, product record, or manufacturer system.

example.value: The manufacturer name 'Schaeffler' in a supplier record.

definition.value: An information content entity that aggregates identifiers, specifications, usage data, condition data, or circular economy information about a component.

example.value: A component record containing part number, material designation, mileage, and reuse assessment.

definition.value: A process attribute that quantifies the travel distance accumulated by a component during use in a vehicle.

example.value: A used alternator recorded with 125000 km of component mileage.

definition.value: A temporal interval that extends from a stated component reference event to a stated observation event.

example.value: A component age of six years measured from vehicle production date to dismantling date.

definition.value: A date value specification that records the calendar year in which a product, component, vehicle, or facility was constructed or manufactured.

example.value: The year 2019 recorded as the construction year of a vehicle.

definition.value: The strength is a material property describing the maximum stress a material can withstand before failure.
The stimulating process is a process describing the application of an external influence, such as force, heat, or radiation, to study material response.
A plan specification that describes the actions, order, tools, and constraints for safely and correctly dismantling a product or component.

example.value: Stepwise instructions for removing a battery module from a vehicle.

definition.value: An objective specification that states an objective for a supply chain process.

comment.en: Bridge axiom for the PMD class stub referenced by the LOG import.

definition.value: A disposition of a product or component to be dismantled under stated technical, safety, time, and damage constraints.

example.value: A bolted assembly has higher dismantlability than an inseparably bonded assembly when reuse is intended.

definition.value: A temporal interval that represents the mean duration of dismantling a product or component under specified conditions.

example.value: An average dismantling time of 12 minutes for removal of a door module.

definition.value: A plan specification that describes how parts are joined, fixed, or released in an assembly.

example.value: A specification that a housing is fastened with Torx screws and snap-fit clips.

definition.value: A plan specification that orders the steps required to dismantle a product or component.

example.value: Remove cover, disconnect cable, release clips, and lift out module.

definition.value: A document or figure that depicts a product or assembly with parts spatially separated to show their relative positions and dismantling relationships.

example.value: An exploded-view diagram showing screws, clips, housing shells, and subcomponents of a control unit.

definition.value: An identifier that records the name of a material sub-group in a material classification scheme.

example.value: The VDA 231-106 sub-group name 'cast aluminium alloys'.

definition.value: A process used to treat a dismantled component, product, or material after removal from its original assembly.

example.value: Mechanical shredding, cleaning, or material separation applied after dismantling.

definition.value: An information content entity that recommends preferred treatment techniques for a dismantled product, component, or material in a given circular economy scenario.

example.value: A recommendation to remove electronics before shredding a polymer-rich component.

definition.value: A software that supports, guides, documents, or validates disassembly or dismantling of a product or component.

example.value: A workshop application that displays product-specific disassembly instructions.

definition.value: A device used to carry out a disassembly or dismantling operation on a product or component.

example.value: A puller tool used to remove a clipped trim component without damage.

definition.value: an intensive quality embodying the total surface area of a material per unit of mass or volume.

An identifier that records the code or number of a material sub-group in a material classification scheme.

A property is a material trait in terms of the kind and magnitude of response to a specific imposed stimulus. Generally, definitions of properties are made independent of material shape and size.
(Callister, W.D., Rethwisch, D.G., Materials Science and Engineering, Wiley, 2014)

Technical materials are complex aggregates. Many properties that are determined for those aggregates are intrinsically associated with the methodologies employed in the measurement process. This is in contrast to typical 'physical' properties, which like e.g. mass that can be determined to high accuracy independently of the measurement process. 
As a consequence, material properties in the ontology are differeciated according to their measurement method, e.g. Brinell hardness and Vickers hardness are different types of indentation hardness rather than different measures/quantification (GDC) of the materials property 'indentation hardness'.
 The 'unit idenifieres' of such properties (e.g. "HV1", "HV10", "HBW") are strictly speaking not units but rather references to the measurement methodology used to determine a numeric value that quantifies the property.
